header.running_head: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abi Taalib (RA) and Other Sahabah (RA) Migrate to Abyssinia and then to Madinah

blocks.text: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abi Taalib (RA) and Other Sahabah (RA) Migrate to Abyssinia and then to Madinah
Rasulullaah ﷺ Permits the Sahabah (RA) to Migrate to Abyssinia and Hadhrat Haatib (RA) and Ja'far (RA) migrate there

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Haatib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I have seen (in a dream) a land of dates. You people should go there." Consequently, (my father) Hadhrat Haatib (RA) and Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) left for the sea and I was born on the very ship (they took)." [^1]

Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Permit me to go to a land where I will be able to worship Allaah without having to fear anyone." When Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted him, he went to Najaashi (the king of Abyssinia). The detailed Hadith will follow soon, Insha Allaah. [^2]
The Quraysh send Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) to Najaashi to Bring the Sahabah (RA) back to them

Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) narrates that a time came when it became too difficult for the Sahabah (RA) to live in Makkah. They were being tortured and put through many difficulties. They realised that these great difficulties and tests were directed at them because of their Deen and that Rasulullaah ﷺ was unable to protect them. Under the protection of his tribe and his uncle, Rasulullaah ﷺ was not suffering as they were. Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore said to them, "The land of Abyssinia has a king who does not oppress anyone in his kingdom. Go to his country and stay there until Allaah creates an escape for you from your suffering."
Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) says further, "We therefore left in several groups until a number of us had gathered there. We had settled in a nice place with good neighbours where we could peacefully practise our Deen without fearing any oppression. However, when he Quraysh saw that we had found a safe haven, they disliked it very much. They therefore decided to send a delegation to Najaashi to have us removed from his country and returned to them. The persons they sent were Amr bin Al Aas and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah. They also collected many gifts for Najaashi and for his generals. There was not a person for whom they did not have a gift that was exclusively for him."
